bottleneck.description: Leading Chinese ADAS SoC + software stack supplier with ~21% market share among Chinese OEMs and embedded Tier-1 design wins across BYD, Li Auto, SAIC, VW Carizon JV; switching cost rises with each model homologation.

dependency.key_customers: BYD, Li Auto, SAIC, GAC, Chery, Volkswagen Group (Carizon JV), Deepal, BAIC, Voyah, plus Tier-1s Bosch, Luxshare, Huaqin, TzTek
dependency.key_suppliers: TSMC (foundry for Journey SoCs), packaging/test partners, IP licensors (Arm, etc.)

editorial.notes: Horizon is the largest domestic ADAS solutions provider in China and the dominant non-Tesla/non-Nvidia compute platform in the mid-tier (36% share at J5 level in 2024), with 290 model integrations across 27 OEMs and a $2.3B VW JV. However, it faces head-on competition from Nvidia DRIVE (Orin/Thor), Mobileye, Huawei MDC, Black Sesame and Tier-1 in-house chips, all of which are validated alternatives. The bottleneck position is structural in the Chinese localization wave (geopolitical preference, software-hardware integration, qualified design wins) but does not approach a sole-source or duopoly status. The auto-grade qualification cycle creates real switching friction once a model launches, consistent with the MEDIUM ALGM/ALGM-style anchor.
